children: Sterling's decline after the Bank of England left interest rates unchanged Thursday reflects the central bank's failure to clearly signal an imminent rate rise, Ebury strategist Matthew Ryan says in a note. The BOE left the prospect of future policy tightening on the table but investors are underwhelmed by the lack of a clearer steer towards a rate rise in November, he says. The BOE remains hostage to geopolitics, and until an Iran peace deal materializes, a policy change is possible at upcoming meetings, he says. Sterling reached a seven-week low of $1.3346 after the decision and last trades flat at $1.3385. The euro hit a one-week high of 0.8592 pounds and is last up 0.2% at 0.8580 pounds. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)
